text:
sam: quick follow-up after the namespace-sharing RFC — thinking about a lighter-weight runtime API for prefix-level sharing that avoids long-lived global leases. rough idea: introduce a short-lived "shadow token" you can pin on request path, validate at read, and allow async rehydrate if token mismatch. thoughts?
cheng: curious — how does this avoid stale reads during concurrent handoff/evict? sounds like another TTL unless token check is tied to eviction epoch.
divya: i like the token idea if token = monotonic epoch per prefix. eviction increments epoch, readers compare. if mismatch: either block (strong) or continue with fallback (eventual).
niko: blocking will kill p95. we'd need to measure. fallback could be a fast shadow read from backing store + async prefetch to cache.
sam: exactly — proposal: token is a 64-bit epoch per namespace stored in residency metadata. API semantics:
```
Cache.pin_prefix(prefix, mode="shadow", expected_epoch=None) -> {token, epoch}
Cache.read_with_token(prefix, token) -> {value, token_valid}
```
this keeps the critical path tiny (one compare) and lets callers decide: block, fallback, or accept possibly stale.
cheng: one compare is fine but eviction must bump epoch atomically with resident->evict transition. otherwise race where evict sets epoch after we've read stale token. that implies eviction needs a small critical section around epoch bump + slab reclaim.
divya: note: we also need a grace-window for inflight requests that hold the old token. bumping epoch should not immediately free KV bytes; set a short grace TTL (e.g., 5s) during which the old epoch is allowed to be served but marked stale in metrics.
niko: ops concern: attackers or hotkey storms could pin tokens indefinitely. we need automatic pin expiry and per-tenant pin quotas. also metric: pinned_count, pin_age_seconds, token_mismatch_rate.
cheng: agree. and surface a new telemetry: epoch_transition{prefix,from,to,initiator} and a small gauge for resident_epoch per shard so we can correlate tail spikes.
sam: tradeoffs: strong correctness requires blocking or global quiesce which is heavy. this approach makes correctness configurable per-client. for control-plane rollouts we can default to fallback mode then flip to blocking for critical paths.
divya: implementation detail — don't bloat page metadata. store epoch in compact header (8 bytes) per prefix + a tombstone timestamp. eviction marks tombstone and bumps epoch in same txn.
niko: can we protomeasure with a canary: 10% traffic to dedicated nodes running token-check path + fallback to cold read for mismatches. collect p50/p95/p99 and extra cost of cold reads.
sam: plan: I'll draft a short RFC addendum with API types + rollout canary plan + runbook for stuck pins. cc @cheng @divya @niko. ops-bot: can you create a canary env? :eyes:
ops-bot: deploy request received: canary-env/kv-token-proto created (id canary-12).
cheng: once RFC addendum exists, also add unit tests for epoch bump atomicity and a small chaos test that kills reclaimer during bump to ensure we never serve wrong epoch.
divya: also add metric alert if token_mismatch_rate > 0.5% for 5m during canary. failure mode will be too many cold reads.
sam: thanks — I'll put the addendum in the RFC thread and link back here. :thumbsup:
